title: Edge-grain cutting board
desc: Glue up strips of maple or walnut, flatten, sand and finish with food-safe mineral oil.

title: Bench hook and shooting board
desc: Two simple jigs that make hand sawing and trimming ends square much easier. Good first projects.

title: Simple step stool
desc: A sturdy stool with angled sides. Practise accurate crosscuts and a strong joint.

title: Dovetailed keepsake box
desc: Cut through dovetails by hand at the four corners. Expect the second box to look much better than the first.

title: French cleat tool wall
desc: Rip plywood strips at 45 degrees and hang them on the wall, then build holders that can be rearranged at any time.

title: Mitred picture frame
needs: Mitre saw or mitre box, clamps
desc: Four mitres that have to close cleanly. A humbling and useful exercise in accuracy.

title: Floating shelf
desc: A plain shelf with no visible support. Finding the studs is half the job.

title: Joiner's mallet
desc: Make the tool you will use for every later project. The handle wedges into the head.

title: Carved spoon
needs: Carving knife, hook knife, green wood
desc: Carve a spoon from a freshly cut branch. No bench and no power tools needed.

title: Bird box
desc: A nest box cut from a single board. Look up the right hole size for your local birds.

title: Cedar planter
desc: A slatted planter box for the porch, with drainage and no finish needed.

title: Pair of sawhorses
desc: Sturdy sawhorses that stack. Every later project gets easier with them.

title: Small bookshelf
desc: Shelves housed in dados so that the joints carry the weight, not the screws.

title: End-grain coasters
desc: Slice and glue offcuts into coasters. A quick way to practise sanding and finishing.

title: Serving tray
desc: A tray with cut-out handles and a rebated base. A good first gift project.

title: Basic workbench
desc: A heavy, flat bench from ordinary timber. Flatten the top by hand as practice.

title: Marking gauge
desc: A shop-made gauge with a wedge lock. Tools you make yourself get used the most.

title: Shaker peg rail
desc: A long rail of pegs for coats and bags, as plain as the originals.

title: Tool tote
desc: The classic open toolbox with a dowel handle. Try nailed rebates at the corners.

title: Chessboard
desc: Glue up strips, cross-cut, flip every other strip and glue again. Accuracy matters at every step.
